```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5,
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

This example shows the steps an assessment working group can take to move an existing JABBA assessment to
JABBA3:

1. run the JABBA reference case (`JABBA::build_jabba()`, `JABBA::fit_jabba()`, JAGS);
2. convert the JABBA fit into a JABBA3 fit object **without refitting** (`jabba2jabba3()`), so that the
   JABBA results can be shown with the JABBA3 plots and tables;
3. **refit** the same data, priors and settings with JABBA3 (`update()`), compare the results and the run time;
4. handle JABBA's diffuse inverse-gamma prior on the process variance, which JAGS can sample but which can
   collapse to zero at the posterior mode;
5. convert and plot a list of JABBA runs.

```{r packages}
library(JABBA)        # JABBA 2 (JAGS)
library(JABBA3)
data(iccat, package = "JABBA3")
bet <- iccat$bet      # catch, cpue (2 longline indices) and se, 1950-2017
```

# The JABBA reference case

A Fox model with the JABBA defaults for the priors, including the inverse-gamma(4, 0.01) prior on the process
variance.

```{r jabba-fit}
jb <- build_jabba(catch = bet$catch, cpue = bet$cpue, se = bet$se, assessment = "BET", scenario = "Fox",
                  model.type = "Fox", sigma.est = FALSE, fixed.obsE = 0.01, psi.prior = c(1, 0.1), verbose = FALSE)
options(scipen = 0)                       # build_jabba() sets options(scipen = 999)
t.jabba <- system.time(jbf <- fit_jabba(jb, ni = 30000, nt = 5, nb = 10000, nc = 2, verbose = FALSE))[["elapsed"]]
jbf$pars[, 1:3]
```

# Convert the JABBA fit without refitting

`jabba2jabba3()` reconstructs the data, priors and settings (`jbinput2jabba3()`) and fills a `jabba3` fit object
with the JABBA posterior: the trajectories as the 8,000 posterior draws of JABBA (`$draws`) and their medians and
95% intervals, the parameters and reference points, and the index fits and residuals as reported by JABBA.
Nothing is re-estimated.

```{r convert}
f.jabba <- jabba2jabba3(jbf, run = "JABBA")
f.jabba
```

All JABBA3 plots and tables now show the JABBA results:

```{r jabba-plots}
jbplot_trj(f.jabba)
jbplot_kobe(f.jabba)
jbplot_fits(f.jabba)
jbplot_residuals(f.jabba, type = "ordinary")
jbplot_runs(f.jabba, type = "ordinary")
jbplot_production(f.jabba)
jbplot_priorpost(f.jabba)
```

# Refit with JABBA3 and compare

`update()` refits the converted object with JABBA3 (RTMB, posterior mode and delta-method intervals); here JABBA's
inverse-gamma(4, 0.01) prior is carried over exactly.

```{r refit}
t.jabba3 <- system.time(f.jabba3 <- update(f.jabba, run = "JABBA3"))[["elapsed"]]
f.jabba3
```

```{r compare}
fits <- list(JABBA = f.jabba, JABBA3 = f.jabba3)
jbplot_trj(fits, type = c("B", "F", "B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"))
jb3_partable(fits, format = "wide")
data.frame(engine = c("JABBA (JAGS, 2 chains x 30,000)", "JABBA3 (RTMB)"), seconds = round(c(t.jabba, t.jabba3), 1))
```

```{r compare-diff}
d <- merge(f.jabba$ts[f.jabba$ts$quant %in% c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"), c("year", "quant", "est")],
           f.jabba3$ts[f.jabba3$ts$quant %in% c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"), c("year", "quant", "est")],
           by = c("year", "quant"), suffixes = c(".jabba", ".jabba3"))
aggregate(cbind(max.rel.diff = abs(est.jabba3/est.jabba - 1)) ~ quant, d, max)
```

JABBA reports posterior medians (MCMC) and JABBA3 the posterior mode, so small differences remain where the
posterior is skewed. For the posterior with JABBA3, refit with NUTS (requires `tmbstan`):

```{r nuts, eval = requireNamespace("tmbstan", quietly = TRUE)}
t.nuts <- system.time(f.nuts <- update(f.jabba, run = "JABBA3 NUTS", engine = "nuts",
                                       nuts = list(chains = 2, iter = 2000)))[["elapsed"]]
jbplot_trj(list(JABBA = f.jabba, `JABBA3 NUTS` = f.nuts), type = c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"))
round(t.nuts, 1)
```

# The diffuse inverse-gamma prior on the process variance

Many JABBA assessments use `igamma = c(0.001, 0.001)`. JAGS samples it, but at the posterior mode (RTMB) the process
error can collapse to zero. `jabba2jabba3()` / `jbinput2jabba3()` therefore replace it by a proxy
(`igamma.proxy`):

* `"posterior"` (default for a JABBA fit): a lognormal prior on the process SD centred on the JABBA posterior median
  of sigma.proc, with `sdb.inflate` (default 1.5) times its posterior log-SD;
* `"fixed"`: the process SD fixed at the JABBA posterior median;
* `"fishlife"`: the JABBA3 default prior; `"igamma"`: keep the diffuse prior (for NUTS).

```{r diffuse}
jb0 <- build_jabba(catch = bet$catch, cpue = bet$cpue, se = bet$se, assessment = "BET", scenario = "Fox igamma(0.001, 0.001)",
                   model.type = "Fox", sigma.est = FALSE, fixed.obsE = 0.01, psi.prior = c(1, 0.1),
                   igamma = c(0.001, 0.001), verbose = FALSE)
options(scipen = 0)
jbf0 <- fit_jabba(jb0, ni = 30000, nt = 5, nb = 10000, nc = 2, verbose = FALSE)
f0 <- jabba2jabba3(jbf0, run = "JABBA")
px <- list(`posterior x1` = update(jabba2jabba3(jbf0, sdb.inflate = 1, verbose = FALSE)),
           `posterior x1.5` = update(f0),
           `posterior x2` = update(jabba2jabba3(jbf0, sdb.inflate = 2, verbose = FALSE)),
           fixed = update(jabba2jabba3(jbf0, igamma.proxy = "fixed", verbose = FALSE)))
tab <- t(sapply(px, function(f){ m <- function(q){ a <- f$ts[f$ts$quant == q, "est"]; b <- f0$ts[f0$ts$quant == q, "est"]; max(abs(a/b - 1)) }
  c(sdb = f$pars["sdb", "est"], K = f$pars["K", "est"], `max rel. diff B/Bmsy` = m("B/Bmsy"), `max rel. diff F/Fmsy` = m("F/Fmsy")) }))
rbind(JABBA = c(f0$pars["sdb", "est"], f0$pars["K", "est"], 0, 0), tab)
jbplot_trj(c(list(JABBA = f0), px), type = c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"))
```

At the posterior mode, a wider prior lets the data pull the process SD further down (towards the collapse the
diffuse prior allows), so `"fixed"` reproduces the JABBA medians most closely; with NUTS, the lognormal proxy with
an inflated CV is the natural choice.

# A list of JABBA runs

Several JABBA scenarios can be converted at once and shown together with the JABBA3 plots and tables:

```{r list}
jbfits <- list(Fox = jbf, `Fox igamma(0.001, 0.001)` = jbf0)
f.list <- lapply(jbfits, jabba2jabba3, verbose = FALSE)
jbplot_trj(f.list, type = c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"))
jb3_partable(f.list, format = "wide")
```
